_comment: What setup installs, as data. The code implements one function per component named here, in this order; tests/test_vocab.py holds the two equal, both directions. Templates are relative to this file's folder. Nothing here may name a repo, a repo path or a repo command (./dev.sh audit content).

components.name: repo
components.installs: for a path that does not exist (or an empty folder whose parent is not in a work tree): the folder and git init

components.name: rules
components.installs: the shared-rules block of CLAUDE.md, between markers; the repo's own sections untouched
components.head: templates/CLAUDE.md

components.name: hooks
components.installs: every file the hooks dependency lists (dependencies.json: its `list --json` over its source; --hooks-from DIR overrides the source): each shared hook and its test in .claude/hooks/, and the shared libraries in the destination the listing gives. Absent: installed; equal by meaning (the dependency's one comparator: comments and blank lines aside) but not byte for byte: rewritten from the source, "header refreshed"; logic differs: drift, never overwritten without --rebuild (no --node), which overwrites it from the source when it is in the rebuild scope (and refuses, writing nothing, while a copy it renders there has changes git does not hold, unless --overwrite-uncommitted); one line per file that differed (`rebuild` below). Without the dependency (a lone clone): only --hooks-from DIR, its hooks folder, byte for byte. Plus .claude/settings.proposed.json for Jacob when settings.json lacks a registration (in a repo setup is creating, that same render is written as .claude/settings.json itself and committed, with no proposal: PLAN-repo-setup §7.9; an existing repo's settings.json is never touched), including (with --plugins FILE) each plug-in hook the registry says applies here: run in place, never copied; with --user-scope FILE (the hook copies report), a shared hook the user settings already run is neither copied nor registered per repo in the proposal ("covered by user scope: <files>"; an existing copy is kept, an existing per-repo registration left out of the proposal so it does not run twice); unknown coverage is never covered. A folder whose .claude/ is its own repo (the workspace top) gets the copies and no proposal (`sub_repo` below)

rebuild._comment: --rebuild without --node (PLAN-repo-setup §7.12, Jacob's yes of 2026-10-05): a file the hooks listing renders into a folder directly under `scope_root` (the listing's destinations: the hooks folder and the libraries' folder) is overwritten from the source whatever it differs in; of the hook files nothing else ever is, and outside them only the parts component's one file (its own entry) (settings.json and settings.proposed.json sit in scope_root itself, not in a folder under it; .githooks/; anything setup does not render). Every hook file that differed gets one line {path, kind, action, detail}, in any run; tests/test_rebuild.py holds kinds and actions equal to what core.py emits, both ways.

kinds.header-only: equal by meaning (the dependency's comparator: comments and blank lines aside), not byte for byte
kinds.logic: differs by meaning: the copy's logic is not the source's
kinds.bytes: differs byte for byte with no comparator by meaning (no hooks dependency): header or logic, not told
kinds.mode: byte-equal, but not executable where the source is

actions.refreshed: rewritten from the source: by construction no logic changed (every run)
actions.rewritten: overwritten from the source (--rebuild only, in scope only)
actions.kept: left byte-unchanged: drift (no --rebuild, or outside the scope)
actions.failed: the write was tried and did not work; the reason is the detail

sub_repo._comment: A folder in no git work tree whose `rebuild.scope_root` folder is one (the workspace top, core.sub_repo; `--only hooks` alone): the copies are rendered and committed there as in a repo, but no settings proposal is written, settings.json never rides the render's commit, and --plugins is refused: what that folder's settings.json must contain has one source of its own, and a proposal would be a second writer of the same file (PLAN-services §3 F3 step 3 (a); Jacob's yes 2026-10-12, su-77 and su-40 2026-10-20). Its registrations are not compared either: that source may run a hook in another way than the hook source's settings.json does, so a comparison would report a difference that is none. tests/test_subrepo.py
sub_repo.note: registrations not compared and no settings proposal written: this folder's settings.json has a source of its own, whose owner registers these hooks there
sub_repo.stale: a settings.proposed.json from an earlier run is here, left as found (setup writes none here; copying it would bypass that source)

components.name: todo
components.installs: TODO.md with the four standard headings, if absent

components.name: docs
components.installs: the repo's docs declaration, if absent: the file the docs dependency's reader names (dependencies.json `reader`), holding a header and each `rows` entry that resolves here (a file on disk or rendered by this run, a glob with a hit), checked by that reader's own parse and resolve. `help` rows run the repo's own command on every read of the index, so they are the owner's to add, never written here. An existing one is the owner's, never edited: it does not parse, or a row resolves to no doc, drift; it lacks a `rows` entry that resolves here, needs-owner. Without the dependency (a lone clone): none, nothing reads a declaration
header: # Docs this repo declares for the shared docs index, one `kind<TAB>arg` per line:
# file <path.md>, glob <pattern.md> (** recurses), help ./<command> --help. Only .md files,
# paths inside the repo. Written once by setup; the owner's from then on.

components.name: check
components.installs: a ./dev.sh stub that FAILS with 'not implemented: fill in the contract' (with --json: the one check schema's red report, check `stub-unfilled`), if absent; never fakes green

components.name: parts
components.installs: the shared suite runner (PLAN-small-tasks §7 step 2) as a rendered copy at `file`: the checks dependency's `runner` (dependencies.json) as its repo's HEAD holds it, byte for byte and mode (an uncommitted edit to it is named in the line and never rendered: another owner's work in progress), so a repo's dev.sh can hand its parts to it (`python3 devtools/parts.py run <parts.json>`). Absent: installed; byte-equal: unchanged; equal by meaning (setuplib/pymeaning.py: the Python syntax tree, docstrings included, since the runner's usage is its docstring; comments and layout aside) but not byte for byte: rewritten from the source, "header refreshed"; meaning differs (an older or edited runner): drift, never overwritten, unless --rebuild (no --node), which overwrites it (refused, nothing written, while it differs from the source and has changes git does not hold, unless --overwrite-uncommitted). Not in the dependency's own repo (it runs the source). Without the dependency (a lone clone): failed, nothing compared

components.name: mutate
components.installs: the one mutant runner as a rendered copy at `file`, into a repo that keeps a `when` file (its mutants; none there and no copy: none, nothing written): this tool's own `source`, as the work tree it sits in holds it at HEAD, byte for byte and mode (an uncommitted edit to it is named in the line and never rendered), compared as the parts runner is: absent: installed; byte-equal: unchanged; equal by meaning (setuplib/pymeaning.py) but not byte for byte: "header refreshed"; meaning differs: drift, never overwritten, unless --rebuild (no --node), refused while the copy differs and has changes git does not hold, unless --overwrite-uncommitted. A copy present is compared whether or not the `when` file is. Not in this tool's own repo (it runs the source). This tool in no git work tree: failed, nothing compared

components.name: services
components.installs: services.json, if absent (PLAN-routing-tree.md §14.8): the skeleton, the repo's name, its `description` (PLAN-architecture.md §9 step 10.2: the one line --description gives; none given: written without one, needs-owner) and its `check` entry (the check stub's command); the owner adds `write` entries and tags. An existing one is the owner's, never written: only its `description` is read, and one missing, empty, not a string or more than one line (or a file that does not parse) is drift; --description is never applied to it. A node's children get none (never guessed). The shared `services-valid` gates the rest

components.name: cli
components.installs: nothing: cli.json ({store, cli, verbs}) is the owner's to write when the repo has a store. No skeleton passes its schema (a store and an executable cli are required), and a repo with no store needs none; the shared `accessor` gates both

components.name: data
components.installs: the store, generated (PLAN-repo-setup.md §7.11): when cli.json declares the import and verify verbs and no path its `store` names is on disk, `<cli> import` then `<cli> verify --json`, run in the repo with DATA_REPO (the data repo's root: --data-repo, else the environment) passed through; installed only when the store is on disk after and every item verify reports is `same`. An existing store is never dropped (part of one present is needs-owner); DATA_REPO unset, or not a folder, is needs-jacob; never in a dry run; the store is not committed; a cli.json declaring no `store` (optional) is none

components.name: params
components.installs: checks.json, if absent: the baseline, no parameter set, so every shared check runs at its defaults where it says it applies. An existing one is the owner's

baseline._comment: Parameters for the shared checks: {"<check>": {"<param>": value}}. None set: every check at its defaults. Keys starting with _ are comments.

components.name: ignore
components.installs: .gitignore with the baseline entries if absent; in an existing one, only the entries git does not already ignore, appended (nothing rewritten or reordered); a negation of one is drift, as is an append that would re-ignore what a root negation keeps (git decides, in a scratch repo; a negation with a pattern in it cannot be tested and blocks the append); a committed file a baseline line covers is drift, never untracked
components.header: # Baseline from the setup tool: its settings proposal, local env files, backups, the shared hooks' run state. Add your own lines anywhere; setup only appends what is missing.
components._entries: line: what is written; probe: a path that line must make git ignore. Present means git ignores the probe through the repo's own ignore files (by meaning, not bytes).

components.name: githooks
components.installs: the git-side gates (PLAN-hard-gates.md §2, §3 rows 3 and 6, §7 phase 2, §7a): .githooks/commit-msg (refuses a commit made in a Claude Code session without an `Agent:` trailer, or with `Agent: jacob`; writes `Agent: jacob` on one made outside a session; writes `check: full | resumed from K/N | none`), .githooks/pre-commit (refuses unless the staged tree is the one the check passed on, and the shared checks' no-secrets is ok) and .githooks/check-pass (the one recorder and matcher of a pass), each if absent; a changed one is drift, never overwritten. core.hooksPath is set only once nothing would be refused for want of wiring: the check records its pass (`record` below, in the check file: a text probe), a checks CLI is configured (--checks, kept in this clone's git config `config` below, never a tracked file), the `stamp` hook is registered, no other hook folder is in use; never in a repo setup is creating (its check is the stub). Another core.hooksPath is drift, never overridden. When core.hooksPath already names the folder, a hook git runs (`runs` below) is withheld, not written, while any of those conditions is unmet: written, it would refuse every commit, setup's own output among them (needs-jacob when the stamp is unregistered, else needs-owner, with the reasons). needs-jacob until settings.json (or user scope) runs both hooks the list below names
components._runs: the files git itself runs by name (a hook): check-pass is called by them and by the check, never by git

components.name: commit
components.installs: one commit of exactly the files it wrote (never add -A, never a proposal): in a repo setup just created, the scaffold, .claude/settings.json among them; in an existing repo, the render (git commit --only), with .claude/settings.json only when it is byte for byte settings.proposed.json; a run that would render into a tree with changes is refused, nothing written; a commit the repo's git hooks refuse leaves the render written and unstaged for its owner (needs-owner)

components.name: remote
components.installs: with --github only: a GitHub repo (public by default, --private on request), origin, and a push of the current branch; verified by the pushed sha and the visibility

components.name: push
components.installs: the push record commit.sh reads (PLAN-services.md §3 F3, verb step 5): git config `config` in this clone, `true` or `false` exactly as the repo's own registration says (the services component's file, its `field`, a boolean: the store; PLAN-architecture.md §13), never from a list here and never guessed. Only in a repo with an origin (none: nothing written, commit.sh pushes nowhere). The registration declaring no `field`, or no registration: needs-owner, nothing written, the current record named (a repo that must not push records false: that is Jacob's call); a `field` that is not a boolean, or a file that does not parse: drift, nothing written. A record that differs from the registration's value (unset, the other boolean, or not a boolean git can read) is set from it, the old value named: the registration is the one source and this record its only writer here. Written at once, never deferred past the render's commit: it gates no commit

components.name: agent
components.installs: nothing: a folder agent is a roster entry, which setup does not own

components.name: server
components.installs: nothing: the group-server entry has no defined shape yet (group servers are not built)

components.name: node
components.installs: with --node only (PLAN-repo-setup §7.5, §7.10): each child node.json lists, set up in turn, created as a repo nested in this one when absent, a child with its own node.json recursing, never with --github; with --rebuild, every file node.json lists as generated, rendered again in place (the setup pass is then a dry run), one line per file (rebuild_statuses); never a record, never a generated file with uncommitted changes
components._render: the components a --rebuild renders afresh, as a new repo in a throwaway folder, for the node's path and name. Not mutate: it renders only beside its `when` file, the owner's mutants, which a new repo never holds, so the throwaway would render nothing (none); its copies are pushed by `setup fanout mutate` instead (tests/test_fanout.py Spec holds every runner left out here to a `when`)

components.name: registry
components.installs: in a node run only, once its children are set up: registry.proposed.json, the union of the node's and each child's services.json keyed by path (`.` for the node), for Jacob to apply to the registry node.json names (as the settings proposal); nothing when it already equals that union. Only the registry's `services` is rendered: its roles and owners have no defined shape here

components.name: gates
components.installs: nothing: with --checks CLI only, and last, once everything is rendered (never in a dry run or a rebuild): `CLI list`, then `CLI run <path>`, then `CLI one <gate> <path>` for each contract gate below that `run` left out (one that applies only under a role, as the audit's), in sequence; their results are this line (a fail is drift, an error or a fault failed, unchecked named). A contract gate not in the list, or reporting nothing, fails the line by name: unchecked, never a pass
components._contract: PLAN-routing-tree.md §14.8: the shared checks beside the contract files

fanout._comment: setup fanout <component> (PLAN-workspace-audit §3.2 option 2, Jacob's yes of 2026-10-13): the components it renders, each into every repo that declares it (`file` present there and, when given, holding `contains`); any other component is refused. The check runs in the repo after the render, the commit only after it passes. tests/test_fanout.py holds `contains` to what the rules component writes, each component here to one setup renders, every rendered runner (`rendered_runner`) to an entry here (its push path), and a runner that renders only beside a `when` file to being declared by that file.

statuses.committed: rendered, the repo's check passed, and exactly the rendered files committed, the message naming the source commit
statuses.unchanged: nothing to render: no check run, nothing committed
statuses.would-commit: --dry-run: a real run would render these files, then check and commit; nothing written
statuses.undeclared: a repo --repos names that does not declare the component: nothing run
statuses.failed: named with why, never committed: refused, drift without --rebuild, a red or unfinished check (the render left written and uncommitted, its paths named), or a commit the repo's git hooks refused

rebuild_statuses.regenerated: a generated file rendered byte for byte, mode included, as the tree holds it (or, absent there, as the last commit does: written back)
rebuild_statuses.drift: a generated file rendered otherwise, or in neither the tree nor the last commit: the render is written and git diff is the finding; one with uncommitted changes is kept, not rendered
rebuild_statuses.record: a file node.json lists as content (or node.json itself): never written
rebuild_statuses.unaccounted: in the tree (tracked, or untracked and not ignored), not under a child, named by neither list
rebuild_statuses.failed: the setup render failed, or setup renders no such file; nothing written for it

statuses.installed: setup wrote it (or, in --dry-run, would write it)
statuses.unchanged: already as setup would make it; nothing written
statuses.drift: differs from what setup would make; reported, not overwritten
statuses.needs-jacob: a proposal was written for Jacob to apply (settings stay his)
statuses.needs-harness: outside setup's lane; the line to add is printed
statuses.needs-owner: installed, but the repo's owner must fill it in
statuses.none: nothing to do: an opt-in step not requested, or a step that does not apply to this repo
statuses.failed: setup tried and it did not work; the reason is printed
